5.2.3
Analysis of the structure of
\Xi^{\mu}
coming from
\mathcal{L}
in eq.(
121
)

Since we have analyzed the total derivative term and the pure gauge term of eq.(
121
) and showed that they are inconsequential, we can finally analyze the gauge invariant term
\mathcal{L}
that truly contributes to the entropy current. Before making the final analysis of the entropy current contribution of the
U(1)
gauge invariant
\mathcal{L}
, we analyze the non-trivial structure of
\Xi^{\mu}
of eq.(
108
). To handle these terms, we must return to the derivation of eq.(
108
). During the derivation in eq.(
106
), we obtained the relation (here
\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial A_{\mu}}=0
because it is
U(1)
gauge invariant)

\delta\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\mathcal{L}+\partialderivative{\mathcal{L}}{\tensor{\Gamma}{^\lambda_\mu_\nu}}\partial{{}_{\mu}}\partial_{\nu}\mathchoice{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}

(129)

which was rearranged to get the value of
\Xi^{\mu}_{\mathcal{L}}
(see eq.(
229
))

\partialderivative{\mathcal{L}}{\tensor{\Gamma}{^\lambda_\mu_\nu}}\partial{{}_{\mu}}\partial_{\nu}\mathchoice{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}=D{{}_{\mu}}\Xi^{\mu}_{\mathcal{L}}+\frac{\mathchoice{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\xi^{{{\lambda}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.74307pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.85834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.04167pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}}{\sqrt{-g}}\partial{{}_{\mu}}\partial_{\nu}\left(\sqrt{-g}\partialderivative{\mathcal{L}}{\tensor{\Gamma}{^\lambda_\mu_\nu}}\right)\,.

Here the subscript

denotes that the

\mathcal{L}
of eq.(

Now comes the crucial point. When we go to the horizon

in our gauge eq.(

), the RHS of eq.(

of eq.(

Hence, in our gauge eq.(

), we must have for some antisymmetric

-symbol

such that

(154)

Thus, we have recast
E_{vv}
of eq.(
122
) in the form eq.(
154
) which is the same as eq.(
10
) with the components of the entropy current given by

\begin{split}\mathcal{J}^{v}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{rv}+\tilde{q}^{rv}+\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right)\,,~~~~~\mathcal{J}^{i}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{ri}+\tilde{q}^{ri}-J^{i}_{(1)}-j^{i}_{(1)}\right)\,.\end{split}

(155)

This is what we originally set out to prove. Most importantly, since we derived these currents from
\mathcal{L}
which is
U(1)
gauge invariant, and we know that
q^{r\rho}
of eq.(
133
) is
U(1)
gauge invariant, the final currents of eq.(
155
) are
U(1)
gauge invariant.

Let us summarize the major steps of our proof. We started off with a generic form of the CS theory Lagrangian given by eq.(
22
). This form, as such, was difficult to work with because of the explicit dependence of the Lagrangian on
A_{\mu}
. We employed the Bianchi identities of the CS theory given by eq.(
109
) to recast the Lagrangian in a form given by eq.(
116
). The explicit dependence of
A_{\mu}
was relegated to a total derivative term and a pure gauge term, both of which do not contribute to the
E_{vv}
of eq.(
122
). The leftover part of the CS Lagrangian denoted by
\mathcal{L}
is
U(1)
gauge invariant but crucially not diffeomorphism invariant. Thus, the
\Xi^{\mu}
term of eq.(
25
) was non-zero. This new structure wasn’t analyzed in
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
;
Biswas:2022grc
because the authors were looking at diffeomorphism invariant theories of gravity. The final structure of
\Xi^{r}_{\mathcal{L}}
was worked out in eq.(
134
). The structures of
\Theta^{r}_{\mathcal{L}}
and
Q^{r\rho}_{\mathcal{L}}
were worked out in eq.(
150
) and eq.(
145
) and they have the same structure as their diffeomorphism counterparts worked out in
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
;
Biswas:2022grc
(eq.(
97
) and eq.(
99
) respectively). Putting all the structures together, we got eq.(
154
), which is what we wanted to prove.

Entropy current for pure gravitational Chern-Simons term:

We remark that if we had considered a pure gravitational Chern-Simons term, we have a significant simplification in the proof. The Lagrangian will already be of the form
\mathcal{L}
with no total derivative term and pure gauge terms of eq.(
121
). Thus, we don’t need the analysis of §
5.2.1
and §
5.2.2
. In the study of the structure of
\Xi^{\mu}
in §
5.2.3
, we only need to prove the linearity in
v
in eq.(
133
). This is done in the first subsection of Appendix
A.5
. Thus eq.(
134
) follows. Since the Lagrangian is independent of the gauge field, we only need to consider the “gravity” terms of eq.(
139
) and eq.(
141
). The analysis of §
5.2.4
simplifies considerably, and we straightaway get to eq.(
154
) resulting in the entropy current structure eq.(
10
).

6

In this section, we will verify the components of the entropy current in eq.(
155
) by computing
\Theta^{r}
,
Q^{r\rho}
and
\Xi^{r}
. We will also show that the final expressions match the brute force results of §
3
. To do that, we first collect the relevant expressions we need to verify the abstract proof. From eq.(
150
), eq.(
145
) and eq.(
134
), we have

These total derivative terms manifest as ambiguities because of our final result for
\Xi^{\mu}
in eq.(
108
) in component notation. Here the derivative with respect to the Christoffel symbol should be symmetrized in the lower indices of the symbol as explained in footnote
34
.
. Thus, for our purposes, we can work with the structures of eq.(
164
). The various structures in eq.(
164
) evaluated in our gauge on the horizon
r=0
become

\begin{split}\mathchoice{\Theta^{{{r}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.34679pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.67627pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Theta^{{{r}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.34679pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.67627pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Theta^{{{r}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.34679pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.67627pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Theta^{{{r}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.34679pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.67627pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}|_{r=0}=\left(1+v\mathchoice{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}\right)\left[\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{r}{v}{x}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.92825pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.34679pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.67627pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1. \makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}}}}h}{2h}\left(\omega+\frac{\mathchoice{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80048pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.00034pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{x}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80048pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.00034pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{x}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80048pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.00034pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{x}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.53473pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80048pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.00034pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{x}}}}h}{2h}\right)\right]+\mathcal{O}\left(\epsilon^{2}\right)\,,~~\implies~~\mathcal{B}_{(0)}=0\,.\end{split}

(166)

\begin{split}&\Xi^{r}|_{r=0}=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\left(\sqrt{h}\epsilon^{rvx}\omega\right)\,,~~\implies~~\tilde{q}^{rv}=-\epsilon^{rvx}\omega\,,~~~~~\tilde{q}^{rx}=0\,,~~~~~j^{x}_{(1)}=0\,.\end{split}

(167)

\begin{split}\widetilde{Q}^{rv}&=-\epsilon^{rvx}\omega\,,~~\widetilde{Q}^{rx}=0\,,~~W^{rx}_{v}=\partial_{v}\left[-\dfrac{2\epsilon^{rvx}\partial_{v}h}{h}\right]+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,\implies\,J^{x}_{(1)}=-\dfrac{2}{h}\epsilon^{rvx}\partial_{v}h\,,\\
W^{rv}_{v}&=\epsilon^{rvx}\left(2\partial_{v}\omega+\dfrac{\omega}{2h}\partial_{v}h+\dfrac{1}{4h^{2}}(\partial_{v}h)(\partial_{x}h)\right)\,.\end{split}

(168)

Thus, the components of the current are given by

\begin{split}\mathcal{J}^{v}&=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{rv}+\tilde{q}^{rv}+\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right)=\epsilon^{rvx}\omega\,,\\
\mathcal{J}^{x}&=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{rx}+\tilde{q}^{rx}-J^{x}_{(1)}-j^{x}_{(1)}\right)=-\epsilon^{rvx}\dfrac{\partial_{v}h}{h}\,,\end{split}

(169)

which matches with the brute force computation of
E_{vv}
in eq.(
40
) and eq.(
41
).

If we evaluate
s_{IWT}
of eq.(
34
), we get

s_{IWT}=-2\left(\partialderivative{L}{R^{v}_{~v r v}}-\partialderivative{L}{R^{r}_{~r r v}}\right)=\epsilon^{rvx}\omega=\mathcal{J}^{v}\,.

(170)

Thus,
\mathcal{J}^{v}
is exactly the Iyer-Wald-Tachikawa entropy eq.(
32
) that satisfies the first law. From eq.(
155
), we see that both
Q^{\mu\nu}
(through
\widetilde{Q}^{rv}
) and
\Xi^{\mu}
(through
\widetilde{q}^{rv}
) contribute to
\mathcal{J}^{v}
and thus to
s_{IWT}
.

Note that since we work with the equation of motion with covariant indices (two upper indices), the match between brute force computations and the expressions of the abstract proof is exact. In the
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
;
Biswas:2022grc
, the authors worked with equations of motion with two lower indices, so the match was up to an overall sign. This is just a convention.

(4+1)D Mixed Chern-Simons term:

We first consider the mixed Chern-Simons term with an anomaly in the
U(1)
sector eq.(
111
):

L=\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma\delta}A_{\mu}R^{\alpha}_{~\beta\nu\rho}R^{\beta}_{~\alpha\sigma\delta}\,.

(171)

Our proof in §
5
relies on transforming this Lagrangian to eq.(

7
Conclusions

In this section, we conclude by summarizing our results and highlighting the crucial lessons from our analysis. Our primary aim in this paper has been to show that the classical second law of thermodynamics is satisfied for dynamical black hole solutions in CS theories of gravity (and mixed gauge gravity CS theories). We have used the setup developed in
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
;
Biswas:2022grc
where the dynamics are assumed to be small perturbations around stationary black holes. To argue the second law, we have looked at the off-shell structure of the EoM (
E_{vv}
) in an adapted coordinate system around the Killing horizon, eq.(
1
). This enables us to obtain the entropy current defined on the horizon, whose components give us the entropy density and a local in/out flow of it on a horizon slice. We constructed a local version of the second law with an extra assumption of the matter sector satisfying the null energy condition.

Firstly, we considered specific examples of Chern-Simons theories and obtained the components of entropy current through a brute-force computation of the off-shell structure of
E_{vv}
. For
(2+1)
-dimensional pure gravity CS theory, the result is given in eq.(
40
), and eq.(
41
), which is limited to linearized perturbations. Furthermore, considering the
(2+1)
-dimensional pure gravity CS theory as a low energy EFT, the quadratic perturbations have been incorporated in the off-shell structure of
E_{vv}
in eq.(
46
), and the entropy current is written in eq.(
47
). In this particular case, we find an example where the second law is established beyond linear order and thus signifies actual entropy production. Next, in
(4+1)
-dimensions for mixed gauge gravity CS theories, working to linearized order in the perturbations, the off-shell
E_{vv}
and the entropy current has been obtained as written in eq.(
60
) and eq.(
61
) respectively.

Once we have obtained these explicit expressions of entropy current for each of the examples mentioned above, we have also explicitly verified that they transform covariantly under a reparametrization of the coordinates maintaining the gauge, eq.(
1
). We have explicitly obtained how the entropy currents change under this reparametrization (see eq.(
76
) for
(2+1)
-dimensional CS theory as EFT, and eq.(
90
) for
(4+1)
-dimensional CS theory). Most importantly, in both cases, we have seen how a non-trivial cancellation was required to assure the covariance as mentioned in eq.(
65
). This also justifies the need to have the spatial components of the entropy current (
\mathcal{J}^{i}
) on the horizon. Interestingly, we have seen for both the
(2+1)
-dimensional and
(4+1)
-dimensional CS theories that the reparametrization may lead to ambiguities in the entropy current components, see eq.(
91
). These ambiguities may be present in the local description of
\mathcal{J}^{v}
and
\mathcal{J}^{i}
; however, they do not contribute to off-shell
E_{vv}
or to the total entropy when integrated over a compact horizon slice.

Next, we have developed an algorithm to construct an entropy current consistent with the linearized second law for a generic CS theory. It is like developing a formalism rather than working brute force with a particular example. In §
5.1.2
, we have shown that the Lagrangian density of any generic CS theory can be written as eq.(
116
). Then, we have extended the formalism developed in
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
;
Biswas:2022grc
to make it applicable to CS theories. We have also used the covariant phase space formalism studied earlier in
Tachikawa:2006sz
;
Bonora:2011gz
;
Azeyanagi:2014sna
to relate off-shell
E_{vv}
with pre-symplectic potential, Noether charge eq.(
31
). We tracked the essential difference between CS theories and diffeomorphism invariant theories: the contribution of the non-covariant
\Xi^{\mu}
(which is defined in eq.(
25
)) to eq.(
31
). By analyzing their expressions in our metric gauge, we finally obtained the entropy current in terms of the elements of covariant phase space formalism; see the final result in eq.(
154
) and eq.(
155
). In order to justify that the technical arguments indeed produce a consistent algorithm to construct the entropy current, in §
6
, we have computed the
\mathcal{J}^{v}
and
\mathcal{J}^{i}
for several examples of CS theories and checked that they exactly match the expressions obtained via brute force analysis.

Some comments regarding further implications of our results and possible future directions are as follows. First, we must note that the setup to establish linearized second law can be used to argue for the physical process version of the first law. Previously, for model-specific theories, this has been worked out in
Gao:2001ut
;
Amsel:2007mh
;
Chatterjee:2011wj
;
Kolekar:2012tq
;
Bhattacharjee:2014eea
;
Mishra:2017sqs
. For arbitrary diffeomorphism invariant theories, this has been established in
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
, see §5 therein, and in
Biswas:2022grc
to include the cases of non-minimally coupled matter fields. Mainly, the off-shell
E_{vv}
as mentioned in eq.(
10
) is sufficient to extend the proof of the physical process version of the first law in CS theories.

It is also straightforward to include a cosmological constant in our analysis. More precisely, the result involving the off-shell structure of
E_{vv}
, e.g., eq.(
10
), remains unaffected due to the inclusion of a cosmological constant. This is easy to understand since the EoM should change as follows
E_{vv}\sim\Lambda\,g_{vv}
, and in our horizon adapted coordinates,
g_{vv}
vanishes on the horizon. Thus, all our results can be directly applied to black holes in AdS space-time. Furthermore, our analysis can be directly applied to any Killing horizons, including cosmological horizons in de-Sitter space-times.

For the examples of CS theories we considered, we see that the JKM ambiguity vanishes, which can be verified from the expressions of
\mathcal{J}^{v}
. For the
(2+1)
-dimensional CS theory, it is zero till the quadratic order, see in eq.(
47
), whereas for the
(4+1)
-dimensional CS theory, it is zero at the linear order, see in eq.(
61
). In the
2+1
-dimensional case, the vanishing of the JKM ambiguity term can be traced back to the counting the number of derivatives in the off-shell structure of the
vv
-component of equations of motion (EoM), i.e.
E_{vv}
. In turn, this is dictated by the number of derivatives present in the Lagrangian of the theory under consideration, which is three in
2+1
-dimensions. Therefore, in
E_{vv}
we should have three derivatives, and hence, in
\mathcal{J}^{v}
there can be only one derivative. From here, it is easy to justify that the JKM ambiguity in
\mathcal{J}^{v}
has to vanish identically in this case. However, this argument based on counting number of derivatives and boost weight will not go through in higher dimensions. On the other hand, in our abstract proof for the generic case, we have not seen any such obstruction, as there is, at least in principle, a possible JKM piece
\mathcal{B}_{(0)}
which contributes to
\mathcal{J}^{v}
of eq.(
155
) through eq.(
150
). It would be interesting to see if the vanishing of the JKM term in our explicit examples is a coincidence or if some universal statement regarding its existence of it can be made more abstractly.

As mentioned in footnote
37
, our algorithm to construct an entropy current is valid only for
U(1)
gauge fields. Since the analysis in §
5.1.2
crucially depends on having an abelian gauge field, it would be interesting to see if our proof can be generalized to include non-abelian gauge fields.

For
(2+1)
-dimensional CS theory, when considered as an EFT, we have seen that the second law can be extended to quadratic order in the perturbations around the stationary black holes. However, recently, in
Hollands:2022fkn
, a formalism has been developed to study the second law to quadratic orders for generic diffeomorphism invariant theories. The result of the
(2+1)
-dimensional CS theory is consistent with Lemma 3.1 and Lemma 4.1 of
Hollands:2022fkn
. Furthermore, the reparameterization of
\mathcal{J}^{v}
for both the theories (see eq.(
77
) and eq.(
91
)) is consistent with Proposition 1 of
Hollands:2022fkn
which previously did not cover the case of CS Lagrangians. It would be interesting to see if Proposition 1 and Lemma 4.1 can be extended to include CS theories. Our analysis in §
5
suggests that at least the linear order analysis (a generalization of Lemma 3.1 of
Hollands:2022fkn
) can be organized similarly to what has previously been done for diffeomorphism invariant theories.

Appendix A
Intricate details of the calculations

A.1
Review of constructing entropy current for diffeomorphism invariant theories of gravity

In this Appendix, we will quickly summarize the major steps in the construction of entropy current for diffeomorphism invariant theories of gravity
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
;
Biswas:2022grc
of the form

L=L(g_{\mu\nu},R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma},D_{\alpha_{1}}R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma},D_{(\alpha_{1}}D_{\alpha_{2})}R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma},\dots,\phi,D_{\alpha_{1}}\phi,D_{(\alpha_{1}}D_{\alpha_{2})}\phi,\dots,F_{\mu\nu},D_{\alpha_{1}}F_{\mu\nu},\dots)\,.

(183)

We argued on general boost weight arguments that structures of
\Theta^{r}
,
Q^{rv}
and
Q^{ri}
take the form of eq.(
96
). To further constrain the quantities in the RHS of eq.(
96
), we must understand the structure of a generic covariant tensor with a positive boost weight. A typical covariant object with a boost weight
w=a+1>0
on the horizon
r=0
takes the form (see eq.(3.13) of
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
)

t^{(k)}_{(a+1)}|_{r=0}=\widetilde{T}_{(-k)}\partial^{k+a+1}_{v}T_{(0)}|_{r=0}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.

(184)

One can show that (see Appendix E of
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
) we can rearrange the
\partial_{v}
derivatives to recast it in the form given by Result:1 (see eq.(3.14) of
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
)

\begin{split}t^{(k)}_{(a+1)}=\partial^{a+1}_{v}\left[\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}(-1)^{m}\,[^{m+a}C_{m}]\,\widetilde{T}_{(-k+m)}\partial^{(k-m)}_{v}T_{(0)}\right]+(-1)^{k}\,[^{k+a}C_{a}]\,\widetilde{T}_{(0)}\partial^{a+1}_{v}T_{(0)}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.\end{split}

(185)

If one includes
U(1)
gauge fields in the analysis, then
F_{vi}
and
F_{ri}
are additional quantities with non trivial boost weights. Thus, one has to include these in the above analysis of eq.(
185
) carefully
Biswas:2022grc
(see eq.(6.17) and eq.(C.8) of
Biswas:2022grc
). Though we mention that eq.(
184
) is valid for covariant tensors
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
, one can check that it is valid for Christoffel symbols as well. For the boost weight argument of eq.(
184
), we can treat the Christoffel symbol as a tensor with one upper index and two lower indices. This is because under eq.(
7
), the Christoffel symbol transforms like a tensor. One can also verify this statement from the expressions of Appendix
A.7
. This will prove to be very useful for the CS theories that we are interested in.

The proof follows by using the general structures of
\Theta^{\mu}
and
Q^{\mu\rho}
derived for eq.(
183
) in
Iyer:1994ys
and then implementing Result:1 of eq.(
185
) in the terms of those expressions. Since
\Theta^{\mu}
is obtained from the variation of the Lagrangian in eq.(
23
), it generically contains
\delta\mathcal{S}_{\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\dots\alpha_{k}}
where
\mathcal{S}
is a covariant tensor. In order to obtain eq.(
31
), we had to use the fact that the variation is given by a diffeomorphism and thus
\delta=\mathcal{L}_{\xi}
. Hence, in order to further process the terms in
\Theta^{r}
, we have to use the input of diffeomorphism invariance to write (eq.(3.23) of
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
)

\delta\mathcal{S}_{\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\dots\alpha_{k}}[\delta g_{\alpha\beta}\to\mathcal{L}_{\xi}g_{\alpha\beta}]=\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\mathcal{S}_{\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\dots\alpha_{k}}\,.

(186)

This implies that the general structure of
\Theta^{\mu}
to be evaluated on horizon adapted coordinates is given by

\Theta^{\mu}=2E^{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}_{R}D_{\beta}\left(\mathcal{L}_{\xi}g_{\nu\alpha}\right)+\sum_{k}\mathcal{T}^{\mu\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\dots\alpha_{k}}\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\mathcal{S}_{\alpha_{1}\dots\alpha_{k}}\,.

(187)

Here
\mathcal{T}
is a covariant tensor and
E^{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}_{R}
is given by

E^{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}_{R}=\partialderivative{L}{R_{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}}-D_{\rho_{1}}\partialderivative{L}{D_{\rho_1} R_{\mu\nu\alpha\beta} }+\dots+(-1)^{m}D_{(\rho_{1}}\dots D_{\rho_{m})}\partialderivative{L}{D_{(\rho_1} \dots D_{\rho_m)} R_{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}}\,,

(188)

where
L
is the Lagrangian of the theory eq.(
183
). The appearance of
\mathcal{L}_{\xi}
in eq.(
187
) makes it clear that
\Theta^{r}
is linear in
v
as in eq.(
96
). One can now implement eq.(
185
) in eq.(
187
) to show that on the horizon
r=0
,

\Theta^{r}|_{r=0}=(1+v\partial_{v})\mathcal{A}_{(1)}+v\partial^{2}_{v}\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\,.

(189)

Here
\mathcal{B}_{(0)}
denotes the JKM ambiguity and it is
\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)
even though it has boost weight zero. This is because the
\mathcal{B}_{(0)}
takes the form of a product of two terms that are individually not boost-invariant:

\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\sim X_{(-k+m)}\partial^{k-m}_{v}Y_{(0)}\sim\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)\,.

(190)

The general structure of
Q^{\mu\nu}
for diffeomorphism invariant theories is of the form
Iyer:1994ys
:

Q^{\mu\nu}=W^{\mu\nu\rho}\xi_{\rho}-2E^{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}_{R}D_{[\alpha}\xi_{\beta]}\,.

(191)

Following this,
Q^{r\rho}
takes the form of eq.(
96
) given by

Q^{r\rho}=\widetilde{Q}^{r\rho}+v\,W^{r\rho}_{v}\,.

(192)

Thus, the divergence of
Q^{r\rho}
on the horizon
r=0
is given by

D_{\mu}Q^{r\mu}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\left(\sqrt{h}\widetilde{Q}^{rv}\right)+\nabla_{i}\widetilde{Q}^{ri}+v\partial_{v}\left(\nabla_{i}J^{i}_{(1)}\right)+(1+v\partial_{v})W^{rv}_{v}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,,

(193)

where
J^{i}_{(1)}
is defined through

W^{ri}_{v}=\partial_{v}J^{i}_{(1)}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.

(194)

We can now substitute eq.(
193
) and eq.(
189
) in eq.(
31
) with
\Xi^{r}=0
to get

\begin{split}2\,v\,E_{vv}&=\left(-\Theta^{r}+D_{\mu}Q^{r\mu}\right)|_{r=0}\\
&=-\mathcal{A}_{(1)}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\left(\sqrt{h}\,\widetilde{Q}^{rv}\right)+\nabla_{i}\widetilde{Q}^{ri}+W^{rv}_{v}\\
&\quad\quad+v\partial_{v}\left[-\mathcal{A}_{(1)}+W^{rv}_{v}+\nabla_{i}J^{i}_{(1)}-\partial_{v}\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right]+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.\end{split}

(195)

Since we have explicitly accounted for all the factors of
v
, we can compare the coefficients of
v^{0}
and
v
of eq.(
195
) to write

\begin{split}\mathcal{A}_{(1)}&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\left(\sqrt{h}\,\widetilde{Q}^{rv}\right)+\nabla_{i}\widetilde{Q}^{ri}+W^{rv}_{v}\,,\\
2E_{vv}&=\partial_{v}\left[-\mathcal{A}_{(1)}+W^{rv}_{v}+\nabla_{i}J^{i}_{(1)}-\partial_{v}\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right]\,.\end{split}

(196)

We emphasize that eq.(
196
) should be thought of as an identity rather than as an algebraic equation equating different powers of
v
. Once the factors of
v
are made explicit, eq.(
196
) holds identically. However, there is one potential source of confusion that we would like to highlight. Apparently, apart from explicit factors of
v
present on the RHS of eq.(
195
), one may consider various objects appearing on the RHS of eq.(
195
) as functions
v
. This may lead to doubting the derivation of eq.(
196
). In §
A.1.1
we will provide some justifications and checks in some particular model Lagrangians supporting the manipulations leading to eq.(
196
).

Combining both the equations in eq.(
196
) we finally get

2E_{vv}|_{r=0}=-\partial_{v}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\left[\sqrt{h}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{rv}+\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right)\right]+\nabla_{i}\left[\widetilde{Q}^{ri}-J^{i}_{(1)}\right]\right)+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.

(197)

Here we have used the fact that crucially
\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\sim\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)
which is

\partial^{2}_{v}\mathcal{B}_{(0)}=\partial_{v}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\left[\sqrt{h}\,\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right]\right)+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.

(198)

From eq.(
197
), we get the components of the entropy current to be

\mathcal{J}^{v}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{rv}+\mathcal{B}_{(0)}\right)\,,~~~\text{and}~~\mathcal{J}^{i}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{Q}^{ri}-J^{i}_{(1)}\right)\,.

(199)

The components of the current are
U(1)
gauge invariant if we consider
U(1)
gauge invariant Lagrangians
Biswas:2022grc
. This is because the structures of eq.(
196
) are
U(1)
gauge invariant. This completes our review of the proof of the existence of entropy current for diffeomorphism invariant theories of gravity.

A.1.1
More justifications and explicit checks of eq.(
196
)

Let us write eq.(
195
) schematically as follows

2\,v\,E_{vv}|_{r=0}=(-\Theta^{r}+D_{\mu}Q^{r\mu})|_{r=0}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})=\mathcal{U}_{(1)}+v\,\mathcal{V}_{(2)}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,,

(200)

where detail forms of
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
are omitted. Note that the last equality in eq.(
200
) is not a Taylor series expansion in
v
. Since
\Theta^{\mu}
and
Q^{\mu\nu}
are linear in
\xi
, it is evident that there are no terms involving quadratic or higher powers of
v
(i.e.,
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
have no explicit
v
dependence), and we can get at most a linear piece in
v
. Then, eq.(
196
) becomes

\mathcal{U}_{(1)}=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2}),\quad 2E_{vv}|_{r=0}=\mathcal{V}_{(2)}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\,.

(201)

Now,
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
should be thought of as structures constructed out of the metric components
X,\omega_{i},h_{ij}
and various differential operators
\partial_{v},\partial_{r},\nabla_{i}
acting on them. While comparing coefficients of various powers of
v
on both sides of eq.(
200
), we are actually working in the configuration space or phase space. For this reason, this is a structural rearrangement of
E_{vv}
, and we never needed to worry about the explicit form of the metric coefficients
X,\omega_{i},h_{ij}
as functions of the coordinates
v,r,x^{i}
for this comparison of coefficients of
v
. Hence for us,
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
are just structures involving
X,\omega_{i},h_{ij}
and their derivatives, and not explicit functions of
v,r,x^{i}
. In other words, we are trying to argue that the relation (
200
) is an identity but not an extra restriction in the the form of a differential equation for
X,\omega_{i},h_{ij}
.

Recently this issue has been dealt in
Hollands:2022fkn
for diffeomorphism invariant theories by using a one parameter family of interpolating metrics
g_{\mu\nu}(\lambda,x^{\alpha})
where
\lambda\in[0,1]
.
\lambda=0
corresponds to the stationary metric
\bar{g}_{\mu\nu}(rv,x^{i})
. The choice of parametrization of
Hollands:2022fkn
is

\psi(\lambda):=\bar{\psi}+\lambda\delta\psi\,,

(202)

where
\psi
denotes the components of metric fields. There the following equation was obtained (see eq.(101) of
Hollands:2022fkn
)

\partial_{v}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}(\ast Q^{vr}_{K}\sqrt{\mu})-v(\ast\theta^{r})\left[g;\dfrac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}g\right]\right)_{\lambda=0}+D_{A}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}(\ast Q^{Ar}_{K})|_{\lambda=0}=2v\dfrac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}E_{vv}|_{\lambda=0}\,.

(203)

Here
\ast
denotes the hodge dual (since
\mathbf{Q}_{K}
is a
d-2
form) and
\mu=h
(the determinant of
h_{ij}
) in our notation for the metric. In
Hollands:2022fkn
the background fields have also been taken as given in eq.(98) by construction. We may think eq.(
203
) to be an alternate interpretation of eq.(
200
) as an off-shell statement in the variational phase space of solutions. In the parametrization eq.(
202
), the interpretation of eq.(
203
) implies that the positive boost weight quantities quantify the tangential derivatives (denoted by
\lambda
derivative in eq.(
203
)) in the phase space of solutions. Once we have accounted for the explicit factors of
v
, we are essentially comparing the variation of quantities in the phase space of solutions on both the sides of eq.(
203
). We mentioned
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
should be thought of as structures constructed out of the metric components
X,\omega_{i},h_{ij}
and various differential operators
\partial_{v},\partial_{r},\nabla_{i}
acting on them. This, in the language of
Hollands:2022fkn
, corresponds to considering the primitive monomials constructed out of the primitive factors. They (
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
) are objects in the configuration space.

It should be possible to formally come up with an extension of this rigorous and formal justification of what we call as comparing structures (not functions of the coordinate
v
) on both sides of eq.(
200
) to Chern-Simons theories. This is because the presence of Christoffel symbols will not affect the boost weight analysis. Since the boost transformation is a linear transformation, the Christoffel symbol
\Gamma^{\mu}_{\nu\rho}
transforms like a covariant tensor with one upper index and two lower indices. The gauge field terms from the matter sector should contribute something new as the origin of boost weight
+1
quantity in our basic building blocks (primitive factors in the language of
Hollands:2022fkn
). This has been the case in
Biswas:2022grc
, dealing with the non-minimal coupling between gauge fields and gravity.

Finally, we would like to provide explicit checks of the identities mentioned in eq.(
201
). First we demonstrate eq.(
201
) in an example of diffeomorphism invariant situation, namely for Riemann squared theory. Next we work out examples of both the specific CS theories that we worked out in this paper. We will show that
\mathcal{U}_{(1)}=0
and
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}
has the entropy current structure for the following examples.

Diffeomorphism invariant Riemann squared theory:

We start with the Lagrangian
L=R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}
. The following objects can be obtained (we refer the readers to
Bhattacharyya:2021jhr
for derivations of them)

\begin{split}\Theta^{r}&=(1+v\partial_{v})(8R_{vijr}K^{ij}-8\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij})+v\partial^{2}_{v}(8\bar{K}^{ij}K_{ij})+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\\
Q^{rv}&=8R_{rvrv}-8v\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}(\sqrt{h}R_{rvrv})-4v\nabla_{i}\left(h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k}\right)\\
&~+8vK^{ij}R_{vijr}-8v\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij}+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\\
Q^{ri}&=4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+4K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k}+4v\partial_{v}(K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k})\\
&~+v\partial_{v}(-4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+8\nabla_{m}K^{im})+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\end{split}

(204)

\begin{split}D_{\mu}Q^{r\mu}&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}(\sqrt{h}\,8R_{rvrv})+\nabla_{i}(4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+4K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k})\\
&~~+v\partial_{v}\left[\nabla_{i}(4K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k}-4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+8\nabla_{m}K^{im})\right]\\
&~~+(1+v\partial_{v})\left[-8\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}(\sqrt{h}\,R_{rvrv})-4\nabla_{i}(h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k})\right.\\
&~~\left.+8K^{ij}R_{vijr}-8\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij}\right]+\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2})\end{split}

(205)

In this case, we have,

\begin{split}\tilde{Q}^{rv}&=8R_{rvrv}~~~~,~~~~\tilde{Q}^{ri}=4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+4K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k}\,,\\
J^{i}_{(1)}&=4K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k}-4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+8\nabla_{m}K^{im}\,,\\
W^{rv}_{v}&=-8\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}(\sqrt{h}\,R_{rvrv})-4\nabla_{i}(h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k})\\
&~~+8K^{ij}R_{vijr}-8\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij}\,,\\
\mathcal{A}_{(1)}&=8R_{vijr}K^{ij}-8\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij}~~~~,~~~~\mathcal{B}_{(0)}=8\bar{K}^{ij}K_{ij}\end{split}

(206)

Thus,

\begin{split}\mathcal{U}_{(1)}&=-8R_{vijr}K^{ij}+8\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}(\sqrt{h}\,8R_{rvrv})+\nabla_{i}(4h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+4K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k})\\
&~~-8\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}(\sqrt{h}\,R_{rvrv})-4\nabla_{i}(h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+K^{i}_{~k}\omega^{k})+8K^{ij}R_{vijr}-8\bar{K}^{ij}\partial_{v}K_{ij}\\
&=0\,,\\
\mathcal{V}_{(2)}&=\partial_{v}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}[\sqrt{h}(-8R_{rvrv}-8\bar{K}^{ij}K_{ij})]+\nabla_{i}(-8h^{ij}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+8\nabla_{m}K^{im})\right]=2E_{vv}\end{split}

(207)

Gravitational Chern-Simons theories in
(2+1)
-dimensions:

We have obtained

2v\mathchoice{E^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}{v}}}}{E^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}{v}}}}{E^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}{v}}}}{E^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.25119pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.55093pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.8221pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{v}{v}}}}|_{r=0}=\evaluated{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{h}} \tensor{\partial}{_\nu} \left(\sqrt{h} \tensor{Q}{^r^\nu} \right) - \tensor{\Theta}{^r} + \tensor{\Xi}{^r} \right)}_{r = 0}=\mathcal{U}_{(1)}+v\mathcal{V}_{(2)}\,.

(208)

For this example we have the Lagrangian

A.2
Details of the calculation of Noether charge for Chern-Simons theories

In this Appendix, we give the details of the calculation of
\Xi^{\mu}
from eq.(

from eq.(

Evaluating

:

The subscript

is used to indicate the variation under the combined diffeomorphism and
U(1)
gauge transformations eq.(

U(1)
gauge structures of eq.(

\partialderivative{L}{\tensor{A}{_\mu}}D{{}_{\mu}}\Lambda=D{{}_{\mu}}\left(\partialderivative{L}{\tensor{A}{_\mu}}\Lambda\right)-\Lambda D{{}_{\mu}}\partialderivative{L}{\tensor{A}{_\mu}}\,.

A.4
The total derivative term of the Chern-Simons Lagrangian

In this Appendix, we will analyze the total derivative term of eq.(
116
) which is of the form
D_{\mu}\mathcal{L}^{\mu}
. While this doesn’t contribute to the equations of motion
E_{\mu\nu}
and
G_{\mu}
, it does contribute to
\Theta^{\mu}
and
Q^{\mu\nu}
. Thus, it may potentially contribute to the entropy current through eq.(
31
). So we carefully analyze this term here. The variation of the action gives

(260)

Hence, we see that a total derivative term has zero equations of motion, but non-zero

Establishing gauge invariance:

We know that
\Xi^{\mu}
of eq.(
261
) is
U(1)
gauge invariant because
\mathcal{L}
is
U(1)
gauge invariant. However, it is not entirely obvious that
q^{\mu\nu}
defined through eq.(
132
) is
U(1)
gauge invariant. This is because we pull out an overall
D_{\nu}
in eq.(
132
). Thus,
q^{\mu\nu}
may not be gauge invariant if we pull out a
D_{\nu}
from
F_{\nu\alpha}
. We thus have to investigate the gauge invariance of
q^{\mu\nu}
carefully. We will prove that
q^{\mu\nu}
of eq.(
263
) is
U(1)
gauge invariant up to a total derivative. The analysis is similar in spirit to how we analyzed the gauge dependent terms in the CS Lagrangian in §
5.1.2
and Appendix
A.3
. The most general form of
q^{\mu\nu}
at the horizon consists of sums of the form

A.7
Useful quantities in our gauge

The gauge choice we work with is eq.(
1
). The horizon is located at
r=0
. The inverse metric components are given by:

\begin{split}g^{rr}=r^{2}X(r,v,x^{i})+r^{2}\omega^{i}(r,v,x^{i})\omega_{i}(r,v,x^{i})=r^{2}X+r^{2}\omega^{2}\\
g^{ri}=-r\omega^{i}\hskip 22.76228ptg^{rv}=1\hskip 22.76228ptg^{ij}=h^{ij}\hskip 22.76228ptg^{vv}=g^{vi}=0\end{split}

(285)

We define the following (extrinsic curvature) quantities:

\begin{split}K_{ij}=\dfrac{1}{2}\partial_{v}h_{ij}\hskip 22.76228pt\bar{K}_{ij}=\dfrac{1}{2}\partial_{r}h_{ij}\hskip 22.76228ptK^{ij}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\partial_{v}h^{ij}\hskip 22.76228pt\bar{K}^{ij}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\partial_{r}h^{ij}\\
K=\dfrac{1}{2}h^{ij}\partial_{v}h_{ij}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{v}\sqrt{h}\hskip 22.76228pt\bar{K}=\dfrac{1}{2}h^{ij}\partial_{r}h_{ij}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\partial_{r}\sqrt{h}\end{split}

(286)

The Christofell symbols for the metric are derived to be:

\displaystyle\Gamma^{v}_{vv}=\dfrac{1}{2}(2rX+r^{2}\partial_{r}X)\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{v}_{vr}=0\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{v}_{vi}=-\dfrac{1}{2}(\omega_{i}+r\partial_{r}\omega_{i})

\displaystyle\Gamma^{r}_{vv}=\dfrac{1}{2}(2r^{3}X^{2}+2r^{3}X\omega^{2}+r^{4}X\partial_{r}X+r^{4}\omega^{2}\partial_{r}X-r^{2}\partial_{v}X-2r^{2}\omega^{i}\partial_{v}\omega_{i}-r^{3}\omega^{i}\partial_{i}X)

\displaystyle\Gamma^{r}_{vr}=-\dfrac{1}{2}(2rX+r^{2}\partial_{r}X+r\omega^{2}+r^{2}\omega^{i}\partial_{r}\omega_{i})

\displaystyle\Gamma^{r}_{vi}=-\dfrac{1}{2}(r^{3}X\partial_{r}\omega_{i}+r^{3}\omega^{2}\partial_{r}\omega_{i}+r^{2}X\omega_{i}+r^{2}\omega^{2}\omega_{i}+r^{2}\partial_{i}X+r^{2}\omega^{j}\partial_{i}\omega_{j}-r^{2}\omega^{j}\partial_{j}\omega_{i})-r\omega^{j}K_{ij}

\displaystyle\Gamma^{i}_{vv}=\dfrac{1}{2}(-2r^{2}\omega^{i}X-r^{3}\omega^{i}\partial_{r}X+2h^{ij}r\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+r^{2}h^{ij}\partial_{j}X)

\displaystyle\Gamma^{i}_{vj}=\dfrac{1}{2}r\omega^{i}(\omega_{j}+r\partial_{r}\omega_{j})+\dfrac{1}{2}h^{ik}(r\partial_{j}\omega_{k}-r\partial_{k}\omega_{j})+h^{ik}K_{jk}

\displaystyle\Gamma^{i}_{vr}=\dfrac{1}{2}h^{ij}(r\partial_{r}\omega_{j}+\omega_{j})\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{v}_{rr}=0\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{v}_{ri}=0\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{v}_{ij}=-\bar{K}_{ij}\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{r}_{rr}=0

\displaystyle\Gamma^{i}_{rr}=0\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{r}_{ri}=-r\omega^{j}\bar{K}_{ij}+\dfrac{1}{2}(\omega_{i}+r\partial_{r}\omega_{i})

\displaystyle\Gamma^{r}_{ij}=\dfrac{1}{2}(r\partial_{i}\omega_{j}+r\partial_{j}\omega_{i})-r\omega_{k}\hat{\Gamma}^{k}_{ij}-(r^{2}X+r^{2}\omega^{2})\bar{K}_{ij}-K_{ij}

\displaystyle\Gamma^{i}_{rj}=h^{ik}\bar{K}_{jk}\hskip 22.76228pt\Gamma^{i}_{jk}=r\omega^{i}\bar{K}_{jk}+\hat{\Gamma}^{i}_{jk}

where
\hat{\Gamma}^{i}_{jk}
is the Christoffel symbol with respect to the induced metric on the horizon
h_{ij}
. The relevant expressions for curvature components at the horizon is taken from
Bhattacharya:2019qal
:

\begin{split}R_{rvrv}&=X+\dfrac{1}{4}\omega^{2}\\
R_{vjvr}&=\dfrac{1}{2}(\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+\omega^{k}K_{jk})\\
R_{vlvm}&=-\partial_{v}K_{lm}+K_{ln}K^{n}_{\hskip 5.69046ptm}\\
R_{rv}&=-X-\dfrac{1}{2}\omega^{2}-\partial_{r}K-\bar{K}_{ij}K^{ij}+\dfrac{1}{2}\nabla^{i}\omega_{i}\\
R_{jv}&=-\dfrac{1}{2}\partial_{v}\omega_{j}+\nabla_{n}K^{n}_{\hskip 5.69046ptj}-\nabla_{j}K-\dfrac{1}{2}\omega_{j}K\\
R_{vv}&=-\partial_{v}K-K_{mn}K^{mn}\\
R&=\hat{R}-2X-\dfrac{3}{2}\omega^{2}-4\partial_{r}K+2(\nabla^{i}\omega_{i})-2\bar{K}_{ij}K^{ij}-2\bar{K}K\end{split}

(287)
